class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Mané Galoyan, Lawrence Brownlee and Nina Solodovnikova perform in “Don Giovanni” at Lyric Opera of Chicago. Brownlee portrays the role of Don Ottavio, the long-suffering fiancé of Anna (Galoyan).</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Cory Weaver</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Soprano Nina Solodovnikova, also making a standout Lyric debut, handles Donna Elvira’s high-flying coloratura passagework with striking aplomb and conveys both the character’s fearless moxie and introspective doubts. With its nuanced, tonal shadings, her hushed, pained Act 2 aria in which she admits feeling pity for Giovanni despite everything is one of the production’s highlights.</p><p>None of the three shows more dramatic range than soprano Mané Galoyan as Donna Anna, who tinges her lower register with shady hues as she mourns the death of her father at the hands of Giovanni but injects a steely tone as she vows vengeance.</p><p>Bass-baritone Christopher Humbert Jr. nicely conveys the confusion and hurt of Masetto and bass David Leigh is suitably stentorian as the Commendatore, the statue that haunts Giovanni and sends him to hell.</p><p>Although it is easy to wish for a bit more vocal power from bass-baritone Tommaso Barea, he maximizes the full comedic potential of Leporello, Giovanni’s hapless, ill-treated servant. Only tenor Lawrence Brownlee seems a little off here, never fully connecting with the role of Don Ottavio, Anna’s long-suffering fiancé.</p><p>Under the impassioned leadership of music director Enrique Mazzola, the ever-reliable Lyric Opera Orchestra infuses vivacity and color into Mozart’s timeless score, with William Billingham on fortepiano and Jesse Langen on mandolin deserving special note.</p><p>“Don Giovanni” was the first opera that Lyric Opera ever presented in February 1954, and the company has reprised it 10 more times before this latest outing, and it’s not hard to understand why. As this latest presentation reconfirms, it is one of opera’s ever-compelling masterworks.</p>

entries.title: Review: Olivia Rodrigo blooms into best version of herself in Chicago performance
entries.summary: <p>Olivia Rodrigo can clearly buy herself flowers. A lot of them. </p><p>On Sunday night, the celebrated singer-songwriter drowned her horseshoe-shaped stage at the United Center with thousands of pink and white stems, probably enough to give one to every fan at the sold-out show. She did for a lucky few as she frolicked around the arena, including doling one out to singer Halsey, who was conspicuously tucked into the crowd.</p><p>All were purportedly fake bulbs, even though the stadium still somehow smelled like a floral shop. And the voluminous props required a road crew of a dozen-plus to fluff and dismantle them throughout each act of the two-hour show. Grandiose? Sure. But it was one of the prettiest transformations of 1901 W. Madison St., serving a larger purpose than just making the arena look like a live-action perfume ad.</p><p>Coming off the massive success of the inaugural Daisy Chain Fields Music Festival in August — Rodrigo’s modern take on Lilith Fair that raised $20 million for women’s and girls’ causes — the music scion has kept the flower power going on her Unraveled Tour. It’s a production that puts femininity and growth at its core, where flowers are both a symbol of love and recognized as the automatic gift that comes at many different life stages.</p><p>For the purpose of this tour — promoting Rodrigo’s latest album “You Seem Pretty Sad For a Girl So in Love,” released in June — the singer took on the stages of a relationship as it mutates from “honeybees” to “maggots.”</p><p> “One of the reasons I’m so proud of [this album] is because I feel like there’s a song on the record for every stage in a relationship,” she explained, describing “Drop Dead” about a first date, “Stupid Song” about being so infatuated you can’t eat or sleep and “Cigarette Smoke” about the resentment you feel after it’s ended. </p><p>The six-act performance evoked this story arc, broken into seasons where Rodrigo (and her flowers) “withered and grew” with each new calendar stage. As Rodrigo's tone changed, the flower crew removed or added bulbs with each turn. She started out confident and boastful in the Spring, where “Drop Dead” and “U + Me = <3” were doe-eyed declarations of young love. But as cracks appeared, “Good 4 U” became Rodrigo’s pungent kiss-off as she stomped through the flower fields in her go-to baby doll dress and pair of Doc Martens.</p><p>By Winter, Rodrigo turned inward, splaying her heart out all over the baby grand piano she commanded for stripped-back takes on “Favorite Crime” and “Honeybee.” (Fake) snow even fell from the rafters above her for effect. But as Winter gave way to Spring again (or, Spring 2 in Rodrigo’s world), the snow turned to rain, which “melted” her dress off during “The Cure” to reveal another frock underneath. And before long, Rodrigo was blooming again, declaring herself an “All-American B----” with a new set of “Expectations.”</p><p>The Unraveled Tour is as theatrical as it is narrative-driven, as Rodrigo continues to develop her storytelling muscle on her third album. But it would be remiss not to think of the evolution of Rodrigo herself coded into this production. At 23, the music star has come a long way from the 17-year-old who burst onto the scene with her breakout hit “Drivers License.” Even she took stock of that Sunday night. “I wrote it when I was a very heartbroken teenager,” she said to introduce the emotional performance. “It’s always fun to revisit those songs as a happier adult.”</p><p>Beyond musical growth, there’s also personal growth where Rodrigo has taken the platform she’s been given seriously as she’s matured. Like her rock heroes Jack White, Hole and The Cure, she puts an activist bent into everything she does, vouching for causes like voter registration organization Head Count and embedding feminist mantras into more than her songs.</p><p>Before she even took the mantle of Daisy Chain Fields Fest, she toured with The Breeders and espoused Alanis Morissette for ushering in this new wave of confessional singer-songwriters (there’s no denying Rodrigo’s “Good 4 U” is the modern-day “You Oughta Know”). She has been a spokesperson for Planned Parenthood and founded her own nonprofit, Fund 4 Good, to support initiatives for women's health, girls' education and preventing domestic violence.</p><p>On her latest tour, Rodrigo has also tapped an exemplary all-women 10-person backing band who brought out her rocker side on “My Way” and “Serena Joy” while a string section ushered in a softer tone on “Begged” and “Cigarette Smoke.” Each date of the tour has also been opened by varying femme-forward acts — in Chicago, the gig went to British rock band Wolf Alice.</p><p>Rodrigo still is one of the hottest tickets in town. But for her and all the young girls who were watching, it’s become more than just a show. It’s about shaping the future long after the curtain has dropped — and for that we<i> </i>need to give Rodrigo her flowers.</p><h3>Olivia Rodrigo set list for Oct. 11, 2026 show at United Center</h3><p><b>Act 1: Spring</b><br>Drop Dead<br>U + Me = <3<br>So American<br>Good 4 U</p><p><b>Act 2: Summer</b><br>My Way<br>Serena Joy<br>Bad Idea Right?<br>Ballad Of a Homeschooled Girl</p><p><b>Act 3: Summer Twilight</b><br>Vampire<br>Purple</p><p><b>Act 4: Autumn</b><br>Stupid Song<br>Maggots for Brains<br>Traitor<br>Happier<br>Begged<br>Cigarette Smoke</p><p><b>Act 5: Winter</b><br>Honeybee<br>Favorite Crime<br>Drivers License<br>Less<br>The Cure</p><p><b>Act 6: Spring 2</b><br>Deja Vu<br>All-American Bitch<br>Expectations</p>

entries.title: Una mujer de 22 años muere baleada en La Villita tras regresar de hacer compras de Halloween
entries.summary: <p>Una mujer de 22 años que recibió un disparo mortal el sábado por la noche en La Villita después de llegar a casa tras comprar artículos para Halloween con su madre fue identificada, informaron las autoridades.</p><p>Abbigail Somoza estaba de pie en una calle en la cuadra 2800 al oeste de 23rd Street alrededor de las 8:43 p.m. cuando dijo haber escuchado un fuerte ruido y luego sintió dolor, informó la policía.</p><p>Somoza, de la misma cuadra, fue trasladada en ambulancia al Hospital Mount Sinai y estaba en estado crítico con una herida de bala en la axila antes de morir más tarde, dijo la policía.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-3b0000" name="module-3b0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Somoza y su madre acababan de regresar a casa después de comprar artículos para Halloween cuando se escucharon disparos desde aproximadamente una cuadra de distancia y Somoza fue alcanzada, según un reporte de policía obtenido por el Chicago Sun-Times.</p><p>Su madre no resultó herida.</p><p>Una autopsia realizada el domingo determinó que Somoza murió por una herida de bala en el torso, según la Oficina del Médico Forense del Condado Cook. entries.title: Nick Lardis reaches developmental crossroads as Blackhawks send him down to AHL
entries.summary: <p>Leaning to his right and watching the puck fly to the left of and behind the goalie from his vantage point, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> winger Nick Lardis thought he might have scored.</p><p>A second later, he realized that wasn't true. He had beaten Islanders backstop Ilya Sorokin's blocker, but he had also missed the net on a wide-open shot from 34 feet out last Thursday.</p><p>Lardis generated two more dangerous scoring opportunities Saturday against the Hurricanes — a three-on-one rush with Ryan Greene and Patrick Kane and a back-door feed from Wyatt Kaiser — but couldn’t bury those, either.</p><p>The offense-starved Hawks would have benefited from Lardis converting one or two of the three chances. And for him to carve out a long, prolific NHL career, he will have to. </p><p>His job is sniper; he isn’t cerebral enough, scrappy enough or defensively stout enough to do anything else at this level.</p><p>On Tuesday, Lardis was sent down to Rockford. The Hawks needed to clear a roster spot for Connor Bedard, and with veteran depth center Dominic Toninato having temporarily secured a fourth-line role, Lardis was the odd man out.</p><p>Given he had averaged less than 11 minutes of ice time during the Hawks' first six games, got dominated in those limited minutes — the Hawks had been outscored 7-1 and outshot 32-20 in them — and wouldn't learn much from sitting out as a healthy scratch, that was probably for the best.</p><p>But the AHL assignment puts Lardis at something of a developmental crossroads. </p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Here’s the video of Lardis’ missed shot last week against the Islanders: <a href="https://t.co/zhMyJm9H90">pic.twitter.com/zhMyJm9H90</a></p>— Ben Pope’s Video Clips (@BenPopeCSTclips) <a href="https://x.com/BenPopeCSTclips/status/2110100182788354111?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 13, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>He crushed the AHL last season, racking up 32 points (including 18 goals) in 35 games, and he'll likely do so again this season. That should help rebuild his confidence, which seems to be a critical ingredient to success. </p><p>He talked about feeling confident during his flash of NHL productivity last spring, potting five goals in the Hawks' final 13 games. He talked about feeling even more confident during his <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/09/20/blackhawks-oliver-moore-nick-lardis-depth-roles-training" >standout</a> training camp in September.</p><p>That made him a popular breakout pick entering the regular season — with good reason. With the narrative having shifted substantially in just two weeks, it's now time to ask some hard questions.</p><p>Will Lardis become simply the Hawks' latest example — replacing Lukas Reichel and, before him, Dylan Sikura — of a small, skilled winger who proved too one-dimensional to succeed in the NHL?</p><p>Or will Lardis diversify his game over time, figure out how to consistently pick corners even on NHL goalies and carve out a unique niche in Chicago? He's not built to be a bottom-six grinder, so it's basically top six or bust.</p><p>Barely a year into his pro career, he certainly still has time to establish himself on the upward trajectory. He has a promising example to follow in Predators-turned-Devils winger Luke Evangelista, who not only <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2025/12/21/blackhawks-nick-lardis-nhl-future-predators-luke-evangelista-consistency" >profiles similarly</a> but is also a good friend.</p><p>And he has the necessary self-awareness of his strengths and weaknesses, too. When I most recently talked with him Saturday, he wasn't shy about critiquing himself.</p><p>"I've got to always be moving a little more," Lardis said. "Sometimes I find I'm caught standing still in the [defensive] zone, and then we get the puck and I'm not ready to anticipate the play. </p><p>"It's pretty simple to say, but when I'm moving and seeing a play evolve, that's when my speed can kill on the ice. Just want to make sure I'm doing that — not just in the 'D'-zone but in the offensive zone, too."</p><p>He also mentioned he needed to defer less to teammates and to attack the interior of defenses more — such as by slashing across diagonally on the rush, as he did to create that look against the Islanders.</p><p>While attempting to earn another NHL opportunity to make those improvements, Lardis should add considerable intrigue to a Rockford team that's otherwise slim on notable prospects.</p>

entries.title: Vatican says the pope has lung cancer and the lower lobe of his right lung was removed
entries.summary: <p>Pope Leo XIV underwent surgery Tuesday that confirmed that he has lung cancer, and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung, the Vatican said Tuesday.</p><p>The tests confirmed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, the Vatican said in a medical bulletin after the surgery. It said the diagnosis had been suspected by preoperative tests and was confirmed during surgery.</p><p>The 71-year-old was in the operating room for about 3 hours, the statement said. The surgery itself lasted approximately 90 minutes. “The surgery was successful, and there were no complications,” the statement said.</p><p>Leo had walked into Rome’s Gemelli hospital through the main entrance earlier in the day and waved to dozens of well-wishers who had gathered to greet him. The Vatican said the surgery would be performed by a team led by Gemelli’s chief thoracic surgeon, Dr. Stefano Margaritora.</p><p>The American pontiff has offered a rare level of transparency about the first publicly disclosed major health problem of <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/hub/pope-leo-xiv" target="_blank" >his 17-month papacy</a>. He revealed the discovery of the small, localized nodule during his Sunday noon prayer and announced that he would have it removed.</p><p>Oncologists said prior to the operation that even if the nodule turned out to be cancerous, Leo’s prognosis is “excellent” since it will have been removed at an early stage.</p><p>The Vatican on Monday canceled all Leo’s audiences through Oct. 20.</p><p>While Gemelli has a specific papal apartment that past popes have used, complete with a private chapel on the 10th floor, Leo will actually be staying in a nearby room since the papal apartment is currently undergoing renovations, according to the Vatican press office.</p>
entries.author: Colleen Barry

entries.title: A few wait-and-sees surround the Bulls as regular season approaches
entries.summary: <p>It is a Bulls offense that is starting to take on the Tiago Splitter philosophy, but far from a finished product.</p><p>Very far at times.</p><p>The first-year coach has made that more than apparent on several occasions throughout the preseason, especially once the transition game is shut down and the Bulls need to generate scoring in halfcourt sets.</p><p>“We don’t have iso players on our team,” Splitter said. “We’ve got to move (the ball). We’ve got to involve more players, pick-and-roll, flare, whatever we need to create action. That’s what we’ve got to improve. We’re far from how we want to play with the quick decisions and quick reactions and better spacing.”</p><p>If that sounds familiar it should as former coach Billy Donovan frequently had that same takeaway when discussing the offense.</p><p>It’s a run-first group that can irritate opposing teams with its athleticism, but when a defense can get back and build a wall, it’s an offense that can get stuck in the mud.</p><p>The remedy?</p><p>First and foremost, keep the ball hopping in the ½-second movement that Splitter has been preaching, right out of the Gregg Popovich school of offense that raised Splitter in San Antonio.</p><p>But there is another. Who is to say that rookie Caleb Wilson doesn’t develop into an isolation player? He has shown an ability to take opposing defenders off the dribble, he has a three-pointer in his bag, and he can also play the drive-and-kick game when multiple defenders gravitate to him.</p><p>No iso player? Let’s wait-and-see.</p><p>Not the only wait-and-see with this Bulls team as the regular season is now just a week away from tipping off in Toronto:</p><p></p><p><b>Pickle with the middle</b></p><p></p><p>The Bulls were hoping to have a better gauge of where they are with center play throughout the preseason, but all they’ve learned is they really have no center. At least not a healthy one.</p><p>Splitter told reporters on Tuesday that Nic Claxton (hamstring) – the projected starting center – was still out and could be out for a while. The likelihood he will be able to practice and then ramp it up in practice to get his conditioning back by next week? Forget about it.</p><p>His projected back-up was Zach Collins and while the veteran was progressing from an injured quad, he has also not played in a preseason game and will have to ramp up his activity.</p><p>Jalen Smith, who actually plays more like a stretch-four, did return from a sore foot, but two-way rebounding machine Tobe Awaka (sore knee) was still sidelined.</p><p>Against Denver, when Smith was resting, Splitter had to go small up front with Caleb Wilson, Matas Buzelis and Leonard Miller. Cute in the preseason but considering the teams the Bulls open up the regular season with it could be tough sledding.</p><p></p><p><b>Battle is over</b></p><p></p><p>The camp battle at the forward spot actually didn’t take too long to solve, and while Splitter won’t come out and declare a winner between Miller, Noa Essengue, and Patrick Williams, he has shown enough of his hand to make that answer obvious.</p><p>Miller has been getting more of the run off the bench of the three, averaging 19.7 minutes per game, while Essengue has been second, averaging 18.8 minutes. Williams brings up the rear with 12.4 minutes per game.</p><p>There’s a good chance that when the team is fully healthy Miller is the only one of the three in the rotation.</p><p></p><p><b>Tre day</b></p><p></p><p>Now that Tre Jones is over a sore hip that cost him playing time, rookie Dailyn Swain can get back to developing as a primary ball-handler rather than being forced into that role as a reserve. If that means playing time in the G League, so be it.</p><p>Will Swain get to that level where he does crack the rotation sooner than later? Just another wait-and-see.</p>

entries.title: Bears DE Montez Sweat suspended 2 games for drug violation
entries.summary: <p>A brutal Sunday for the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> has bled into an even worse week.</p><p>Defensive end Montez Sweat, who is the Bears’ highest-paid player this season, was suspended two games by the NFL on Tuesday for violating its performance-enhancing drug policy. He will miss Sunday’s game in Atlanta and the Bears’ “Thursday Night Football” home game against the Patriots before being reinstated Oct. 23. Those games carry extra importance for a Bears team that, despite being 3-2, sits at the bottom of the NFC North.</p><p>Sweat’s absence in a blow for the Bears in the wake of their 31-7 shellacking at the hands of the rival Packers on Sunday Lambeau Field. It’s also a dent in the culture established by general manager Ryan Poles, who traded for Sweat three years ago, and second-year head coach Ben Johnson. The culture, and Johnson’s sheer force of personality, was often credited for the Bears’ success last season, when they won the NFC North and their first playoff game in 15 years.</p><p>Sweat had a team-high 10 sacks last season in what Johnson considered the best season of the defensive end’s career.</p><p>He has two sacks and seven tackles this season. His absence, though, is crushing for a position group that is considered the most shallow on the team. Poles and Johnson did not draft, sign or trade for significant help at the position last offseason despite speaking openly about their need to improve their pass rush in Year 2 under coordinator Dennis Allen.</p><p>The defensive end position has thinned out in recent days, too. One week ago, veteran Marcus Davenport abruptly retired one day after making his Bears debut, playing 12 snaps against the Jets. The former first-round pick had been on the team’s practice squad, but the Bears were optimistic he’d be able to contribute off their bench. Sunday, defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo — who had one sack per game over the previous three — left <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/12/bears-packers-ben-johnson-loss-disconcerting-beyond-nfc-rivalry-nfc-north-dennis-alllen-nfl-head-coach-thanksgiving" target="_blank" >the loss to the Packers</a> with a quad injury.</p><p>Defensive end Austin Booker sacked Packers quarterback Jordan Love twice, both near the end of the first half, and led his position by playing 72% of the Bears’ snaps. James Lynch, who is considered a solid run defender, started and played 27 snaps Sunday. He can play either tackle or end.</p><p>The Bears will get a boost at the position this week. They activated Shemar Turner, their former second-round pick, from the physically-unable-to-perform list. He's recovered from a torn ACL suffered in the middle of last season.</p><p>Poles traded a second-round pick to the Commanders for Sweat three years ago and days later gave him a four-year, $98 million contract extension. He is the team's highest-paid player this season, posting a $25.08 million salary cap. He is due a $2 million roster bonus on the fifth league day of next year, which gives the Bears a deadline to decide whether or not they want to bring him back for the last year of his contract. He has a dead cap charge of only about $4 million next year, and the Bears don't owe him any further guaranteed money.</p>
entries.author: Patrick Finley

entries.title: Juez ordena mantener detenida a mujer ‘tan peligrosa’ acusada de matar a una niña de 7 años en Chicago
entries.summary: <p>Una mujer acusada de apuñalar mortalmente a una niña de 7 años permaneció detenida el viernes, mientras los seres queridos de la menor llenaban una sala de corte del Condado de Cook para una audiencia inicial enfocada en el brutal ataque y el historial de enfermedad mental severa de la acusada.</p><p>El juez del circuito del Condado de Cook, John Hock, determinó que Shavon Gayden era “tan peligrosa como puede ser una persona”, y luego ordenó que permaneciera recluida en la Cárcel del Condado de Cook. Gayden, de 48 años, enfrenta un cargo de asesinato en primer grado por la <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/10/07/mujer-acusada-matar-tiene-antecedentes-ataques-violentos" target="_blank" >muerte de Eddimar Hernández Chacón</a> la semana pasada.</p><p>La familia de Eddimar vistió camisetas con su foto y escuchó atentamente mientras los fiscales describían el “ataque brutal y malvado contra una niña de 7 años”.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-670000" name="module-670000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Eddimar y su hermana mayor caminaban por la cuadra 8600 al sur de Cottage Grove alrededor del mediodíadel 3 de octubre cuando Gayden empezó a correr hacia ellas con el brazo levantado, dijo en corte el viernes el fiscal adjunto Mike Pekara.</p><p>Gayden primero se abalanzó sobre la hermana, luego agarró a Eddimar, la tiró al suelo y comenzó a apuñalarla, dijo Pekara.</p><p>La hermana gritó pidiendo auxilio mientras Eddimar caía en sus brazos y Gayden se alejaba de la escena, según Pekara. Eddimar sufrió cuatro puñaladas en la espalda y fue declarada muerta poco después en el Hospital Infantil Comer.</p><p>Tres de los cuatro arrestos previos de Gayden también involucraron cuchillos, según Pekara y los registros judiciales.</p><p>Antes del ataque del sábado, Gayden estaba adentro de una tienda en la Avenida Cottage Grove tratando de pagar su factura de celular cuando se puso “impaciente” con los empleados y amenazó con apuñalar a uno en el cuello, dijo Pekara.</p><p>“El cuchillo es su instrumento de muerte, su instrumento de violencia, su instrumento de agresión”, dijo Pekara. “La violencia que ejerció sobre esa niña fue... impredecible”.</p><p>Hock ordenó el viernes que Gayden permanezca detenida mientras avanza el caso, citando su historial violento y sus “graves problemas de salud mental”. También ordenó una evaluación psiquiátrica.</p><p>“Ahora ha demostrado que atacará y potencialmente matará a uno de los miembros más vulnerables de nuestra sociedad”, dijo Hock. “Es tan peligrosa como puede ser una persona, muy probablemente debido a serios problemas de salud mental”.</p><p>El abogado de Gayden, el defensor público adjunto Brett Balmer, no se opuso a la petición de Pekara para la detención. Balmer le dijo a la corte que estaba de acuerdo en que Gayden debía seguir bajo custodia y bajo el cuidado de un médico.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" vivienda.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Anthony Vazquez/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>“Obviamente no está en condiciones de salir a la calle”, dijo Balmer a los reporteros después de la audiencia. “Como indiqué el lunes, está en medio de una grave crisis psiquiátrica y necesita ayuda”.</p><p>Balmer dijo que su clienta ha luchado con enfermedad mental y la falta de vivienda, y señaló que Gayden “vivía en la calle”. Pero Balmer rechazó la caracterización de los fiscales de Gayden como “malvada”.</p><p>“Yo respondería diciendo que ella está mentalmente enferma”, dijo Balmer. “Eso no es lo mismo. He atendido a muchos clientes con enfermedades mentales y casos muy, muy horribles, como este. Es trágico. Es desgarrador”.</p><p>La salud mental de Gayden comenzó a deteriorarse hace unos 10 años, pero “nunca recibió la atención psiquiátrica que necesitaba”, según Balmer.</p><p>En 2016, Gayden fue arrestada por apuñalar a su novio con un “cuchillo pequeño”, según Pekara. Fue arrestada de nuevo en 2019 por correr hacia su hijo con un cuchillo. Ambos casos fueron desestimados después de que las víctimas no se presentaran ante la corte.</p><p>Luego, Gayden fue acusada de golpear a una empleada de la Autoridad de Tránsito de Chicago (CTA) en 2023 y amenazarla con apuñalarla, muestran los registros judiciales. Se recuperaron tres cuchillos de su bolso. Más tarde se declaró culpable de esos cargos en 2024 y recibió dos años de libertad condicional.</p><p>Aproximadamente un mes después de ese acuerdo, fue arrestada de nuevo por atacar a una empleada de un albergue. Luego, Gayden dejó de presentarse ante la corte en el caso de la CTA y el año pasado se emitió una orden de arresto en su contra, según los registros judiciales.</p><p>La orden seguía vigente cuando fue arrestada el sábado.</p><p>Balmer dijo que la madre de Gayden está devastada por lo ocurrido “a manos de su hija”. La madre de Gayden ha dicho repetidamente que “esto no hubiera pasado” si su hija hubiera recibido la ayuda que necesitaba, según Balmer.</p><p>“Creo que usó las palabras ‘una bomba de tiempo a punto de estallar’”, añadió Balmer.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de</i> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a><br></p>

entries.title: Mayor Johnson says public desire to ramp up taxes on big corporations affirmed by survey results
entries.summary: <p>Nearly 90% of Chicagoans surveyed want to tax corporations to expand city services, Mayor Brandon Johnson said Tuesday, promising to deliver what he can locally while asking the state to empower the city to impose more business taxes.</p><p>Johnson released a “budget engagement report” that he believes strengthens his hand in the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/09/28/city-council-opposition-pre-election-budget-battle-mayor-brandon-johnson" >battle for a pre-election budget </a>with the renegade City Council majority that rejected his corporate head tax a year ago.</p><p>Of the 591 survey responses generated at five events across the city, 88% of those surveyed wanted the city to raise taxes on large corporations. No other options got more than 50% support, the mayor said.</p><p>Johnson vowed to "pursue the progressive revenue that’s needed to deliver" on those priorities. </p><p>“What remains to be seen is whether the corporate-aligned caucus will have the collective courage to choose the interests and priorities of Chicagoans, or choose to cower before the influence and campaign donations of corporations,” Johnson said.</p><p>Eight days before unveiling his 2026 budget, Johnson dropped his strongest hint yet that he would erase an $882.4 million budget shortfall by raising the same technology taxes he imposed last year to start shifting Chicago’s outdated tax structure to accommodate the digital economy.</p><p>Those taxes include the personal property lease transaction tax; applying the 10.25% amusement tax on sports bets and a tax on social media companies that is still the subject of a court challenge</p><p>The personal property lease transaction tax on vehicle and equipment rentals, car leases and cloud computing software was 11% just two years ago. It was raised to 15% last year and had already generated $737.6 million by August, exceeding expectations by $23 million.</p><p>The groundbreaking tax on social media is also doing nearly 60% better than expected, even though the windfall is being held in escrow.</p><p>Asked what taxes he could impose on corporations beyond renewing his failed fight for the corporate head tax, Johnson said the city’s power to impose business taxes is limited by state law.</p><p>“Our work should be centered around, not only challenging the ultra-rich and big corporations to pay their fair share, but… if the state of Illinois is not prepared to do that, then give me and other municipalities the authority to do it ourselves,” the mayor said.</p><p>Johnson said Chicagoans have “given me a mandate” to preserve and enhance the city services they depend on. But the state of Illinois “takes that authority away from the city of Chicago and other municipalities."</p><p>“That’s why I believe that, if the state of Illinois is not prepared to do that, then they should provide local municipalities with the authority to find ways outside of PPLT, to find ways outside of the social media (tax) even when we’re talking about how we generate revenue from sports and gaming. These are corporations that have the responsibility to put skin in the game, but those limitations are what they are. They're real," he said.</p><p>The home rule authority that gives Chicago broad power to govern itself dates back to 1970 when Illinois adopted a state constitution.</p><p>It designated Illinois cities with more than 25,000 residents as home rule units and gave those cities broad powers to incur debt and to tax, regulate and license themselves without state approval.</p><p>But there are limits to that authority. Chicago can levy certain local taxes without state legislation or voter approval, but not others. An example was Johnson’s signature “Bring Chicago Home” proposal to raise the tax on high-end real estate transactions to generate $100 million a year to combat homelessness.</p><p>The mayor’s preferred option was to convince state lawmakers to raise the real estate transfer tax. When lawmakers refused and Gov. JB Pritzker gave the proposal the cold shoulder, Johnson had to seek approval from Chicago voters. The referendum failed after a big bucks campaign by real estate and business interests.</p><p>The limits to Chicago’s home rule powers also explain why the perennial idea of extending the state sales tax to professional services — with a potential annual yield of $305 million for Chicago — has gone nowhere for decades. It needs legislative approval and, so far, hasn’t gotten it.</p><p>Legislative approval would also likely be needed to impose the corporate payroll tax championed by the so-called “Institute for the Public Good,” a group of mayoral allies behind the failed “Bring Chicago Home” referendum.</p><p>The group has claimed that asking corporations with “more than $8 million” in annual payroll to pay 5% of salaries paid to employees earning more than $200,000 a year could generate a $1.5 billion annual windfall for the city.</p>

entries.title: Mike Ditka a bigger star than Michael Jordan? Well, yeah, for a little while
entries.summary: <p>ESPN’s Mike Greenberg might have overseasoned things just a little.</p><p>Paying on-air tribute to Mike Ditka, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/09/da-coach-mike-ditka-embodied-chicago-city-he-adopted" target="_blank" >who died Friday at 86</a>, Greenberg (ahem, no relation) talked about arriving on the Chicago media scene in 1992 before Ditka’s final season as <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> coach.</p><p>“The truth of the matter is Michael Jordan was a global icon and certainly beloved in Chicago, but Mike Ditka was the biggest star in Chicago sports,” he said. “And, in my opinion, it’s inarguable.”</p><p>It’s plenty arguable. And this being America in 2026, when the very most important thing a person can do is wail like a banshee on social media, more than enough people to pack Soldier Field argued with Greenberg’s premise as though the man had committed an act of unspeakable evil. Treasonous, for sure. Probably worse.</p><p>Jordan was our No. 1 star, was their point. And they were right. By the time Jordan started hanging banners, everyone else, Ditka included, was in the recesses of his immense shadow.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">"He was larger than life. ... Michael Jordan was a global icon and certainly beloved in Chicago, but Mike Ditka was the biggest star in Chicago sports."<a href="https://x.com/Espngreeny?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">@Espngreeny</a> explains how much of an impact Mike Ditka had on the city of Chicago 🙌<br><br>(via <a href="https://x.com/PatMcAfeeShow?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">@PatMcAfeeShow</a>) <a href="https://t.co/TUxXkuOPGK">pic.twitter.com/TUxXkuOPGK</a></p>— SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) <a href="https://x.com/SportsCenter/status/2108623881275629676?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 9, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>But what Greenberg said about Ditka wasn’t far off in terms of time. A handful of years earlier, at what absolutely was — and still is — the historical zenith of our sports scene, Ditka still loomed largest.</p><p>For a time in the 1980s, everything here was popping all at once. The Blackhawks reached the conference finals three times from 1982 to 1985. The White Sox won 99 games in 1983 to reach the postseason for the first time since the 1959 World Series. The 1984 Cubs won 96 games and played October baseball for the first time since the 1945 World Series. That year — 1984 — started with Illinois in the Rose Bowl and its men’s basketball team en route to a Big Ten title and the Elite Eight, while DePaul’s hoopers soared to a No. 2 national ranking. And then, by God, the Bulls drafted Jordan. We were the luckiest sports fans on Earth.</p><p>Meanwhile, Ditka’s 1984 Bears dramatically upped the ante, going 7-1 in the NFC Central and piling up a dizzying 72 sacks, still the NFL record. That year was the first of five straight division titles for the Bears, who, of course, sent things into the stratosphere as the Super Bowl champs of the 1985 season. All the pro teams in town had big stars — the Bears had lots of them — but Ditka was the celebrity-in-chief and remained so through close to the end of the decade. That’s my story, anyway, and I’m sticking to it.</p><p>Jordan overtook Ditka before long, no doubt, and by a lot. His Airness was transcendent and celestial; Ruthian; Bird, Magic and Dr. J put together and then some.</p><p>Greenberg was flat wrong. But he was also almost right.</p><h3><b>Lots to un-Pack</b></h3><p>Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said last week, “When you play [cornerback] in this scheme, it’s like being a window washer on a high-rise building — you can’t make mistakes.”</p><p>Cue the parade of mistakes against the Packers, who feasted on deep shots, connecting for gains of 31, 36, 42, 46, 50 and 53 yards. Some of that was quarterback Jordan Love’s elite accuracy on deep balls in general, but let’s not sugarcoat it — the Bears have coverage issues.</p><p>Wide receiver Christian Watson had a giant game and saw it coming.</p><p>“A hundred percent,” Watson said afterward, beaming and flashing a sparkling grill. “I got called crazy for thinking we could exploit the defense [as much as we did] and put up a lot of points against them, but we watched the film; we saw opportunities there. Regardless of how good they were in other games against certain teams, we knew what was going to be there and took advantage.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div Oct. 11, 2026.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Matt Ludtke/AP </p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p></p><h3><b>Ben-o-meter: 4 out of 10</b></h3><p>It suddenly seems Ben Johnson is up against it, doesn’t it? He has to ease QB Caleb Williams back in — hopefully this week — in order to protect Williams from further injury. He has to decide whether or not to demote backup Tyson Bagent. He has to worry about his running game, with Kyle Monangai’s turf toe ongoing and Roschon Johnson not having impressed in Green Bay. He has to face having been outfoxed by Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores and outdone by Packers head coach Matt LaFleur in all-important division games. He can’t feel too good about his defense.</p><p>Other than that, though, everything’s peachy.</p><h3><b>Look who’s coming: the Falcons</b></h3><p>Which Falcons will the Bears get Sunday in Atlanta? The ones who scored 56 fewer points against the Panthers than the Bears did? Or the ones who won 35-14 at Lambeau Field?</p><p>It doesn’t work like that, of course. The sick, twisted truth is nobody knows how any team is going to play pretty much ever. It’s especially true in the case of the Falcons, who have one QB, Michael Penix Jr., dealing with a rib injury and another, Tua Tagovailoa, who is battling a nagging case of being Tua Tagovailoa. One expects the Bears will have to survive a mountainous dose of Bijan Robinson, maybe the best running back in the NFL.</p><p>Atlanta does rank No. 4 in the league against the run, an impressive stat, but is No. 27 against the pass. Former Bears defensive tackle Gervon Dexter is coming off his best game with his new team, having stuffed three running plays at or behind the line of scrimmage against Derrick Henry and the Ravens.</p><h3><b>Take the North</b></h3><p>With the Vikings at 5-0 and the rest of the division’s teams tied at 3-2, what’s the real pecking order through five weeks?</p><p><b>1. Vikings: </b>But you knew that already.</p><p><b>2. Lions: </b>Johnson’s current team isn’t about to set any NFL scoring records, but his former team might.</p><p><b>3. Packers: </b>Easy, Cheesies, you’ve still got plenty to prove.</p><p><b>4. Bears: </b>Just saying, there’s no such thing as winning the division with a losing division record two years in a row.</p>

entries.title: Investigación de presunto contacto inapropiado de candidato a presidente de la Junta de CPS y una menor podría concluir pronto
entries.summary: <p>La inspectora general de las Escuelas Públicas de Chicago (CPS) podría emitir pronto conclusiones en su investigación, reabierta recientemente, sobre si Hilario Domínguez, candidato a la presidencia de la Junta Escolar de Chicago, actuó de manera inapropiada con una joven de 17 años en 2017.</p><p>Los investigadores entrevistaron a la mujer, que ahora tiene 26 años de edad, a finales de septiembre y volvieron a entrevistar a Domínguez el martes.</p><p>La mujer le dijo al Chicago Tribune y a otros medios de comunicación que Domínguez le preguntó sobre su vida amorosa mientras estaban solos en un carro, y que en una ocasión la alzó con un abrazo y la hizo girar.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-970000" name="module-970000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>En ese momento, Domínguez tenía 24 años y trabajaba como organizador en el Proyecto Resurrección, una organización sin fines de lucro con sede en Pilsen, mientras ella era una estudiante de CPS que trabajaba allí mediante el programa de empleos de verano de la Ciudad.</p><p>La mujer dijo a Chalkbeat y Block Club Chicago que el abrazo, con su cuerpo pegado al de él, la hizo sentir “muy incómoda” y que el episodio en el carro fue “realmente alarmante” porque Domínguez “era una figura de autoridad en la que yo confiaba”. También dijo que el comportamiento preocupante se detuvo después de que ella se quejó con un empleado adulto.</p><p>Según varias fuentes, la joven tiene vínculos personales con la antigua rival política de Domínguez, Aída Flores. Domínguez niega las acusaciones y dice que tienen motivaciones políticas.</p><p>“Para mí, esto va más allá de una campaña política”, dijo a WBEZ. “Esto tiene que ver con cómo mantengo la frente en alto en los vecindarios y en la ciudad que me crió”.</p><p>La oficina del inspector general del distrito escolar abrió por primera vez una investigación sobre los supuestos incidentes en 2021, cuando Domínguez enseñaba en CPS. Dejó ese puesto en 2022 para trabajar como subdirector político del Sindicato de Maestros de Chicago (CTU), que respaldó a Domínguez en la contienda por la junta escolar.</p><p>A principios de este año, la oficina del inspector general determinó que las acusaciones no estaban fundamentadas, según un correo electrónico enviado por un investigador a Domínguez y revisado por WBEZ. Pero la oficina reabrió recientemente el caso.</p><p>El inspector general Philip Wagenknecht no quiso comentar por qué, pero la mujer le dijo al Tribune que se comunicó con su oficina porque no fue entrevistada para la investigación original.</p><p>Estas acusaciones han quedado en medio de la intensa <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/graphics/chicago-school-board-education-voter-guide/es/school-board/president/" target="_blank" >contienda por la presidencia de la junta escolar</a> en Chicago.</p><p>Jessica Biggs, una de las rivales de Domínguez en la carrera, dijo que la supuesta conducta era “profundamente preocupante” y que las mujeres y las niñas en CPS están prestando atención.</p><p>“Se merecen saber que la próxima persona al frente de la Junta de Educación de CPS tomará en serio sus experiencias”, dijo.</p><p>Una de las colaboradoras de Biggs, Alaina Hampton, dijo en un comunicado que conoce a la mujer desde hace años y que estaba al tanto de las acusaciones desde hace mucho tiempo. Hampton dijo que la mujer se puso en contacto con ella a principios de septiembre, cuando el inspector general le informó que el caso había sido cerrado.</p><p>Hampton le recomendó a la mujer que contratara a un abogado. Hampton dijo que “seguirá solidarizándose con las víctimas y sobrevivientes”.</p><p>Hampton formó parte de una demanda de acoso sexual de alto perfil presentada en 2018 contra el Partido Demócrata de Illinois y otros. <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2019/11/29/20988763/alaina-hampton-federal-lawsuit-madigan-quinn-settlement" target="_blank" >Llegó a un acuerdo en ese caso</a>.</p><p>A través de su abogado, la mujer se negó a responder preguntas de WBEZ. Pero ha dicho que ahora está hablando porque quería contar su propia historia. Dijo a NBC Chicago que las interacciones de Domínguez con ella deberían descalificarlo para servir como presidente de la junta escolar.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Personas se reunieron durante una conferencia de prensa afuera de The Resurrection Project en 2023. Una mujer alega que Hilario Dominguez tuvo un comportamiento inapropiado con ella cuando trabajaba en la organización sin fines de lucro con sede en Pilsen a través de un programa de empleos de verano en 2017.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Anthony Vazquez/Sun-Times file</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Domínguez dejó el Proyecto Resurrección en 2018 para postularse a concejal del distrito 25. Flores, subdirectora en CPS, fue una de cuatro opositoras esa vez.</p><p>Domínguez dice que estas acusaciones surgieron por primera vez durante esa campaña. Ambos perdieron.</p><p>Cuando Flores se postuló por segunda vez en 2023, contó con el respaldo de un comité de acción política (PAC) que se opone a CTU. El sitio web de la campaña de Flores dice que está recolectando firmas para volver a postularse en febrero.</p><p>Flores dijo en un correo electrónico a WBEZ que no hablaría del tema mientras la investigación del inspector general está en curso. A principios de esta semana, Flores dijo a Chalkbeat y Block Club que no estuvo involucrada en sacar a la luz las acusaciones.</p><p>Domínguez insiste en “que no tuvo ese tipo de interacciones” con la mujer.</p><p>También dijo que cree que la conducta sexual inapropiada debe tomarse en serio.</p><p>Paloma Rodríguez, excoordinadora de vivienda del Proyecto Resurrección, dijo a WBEZ que envió correos electrónicos en 2017 para informar a la gerencia superior que la joven se sentía incómoda cerca de Domínguez.</p><p>Cuando Domínguez anunció que se lanzaría a la política en 2018, dijo que decidió hablar “más fuerte” sobre la supuesta conducta. Presentó un reporte de policía a la gerencia superior en diciembre de 2018, según una copia censurada revisada por WBEZ. Rodríguez dijo a WBEZ que también lo escribió para cubrirse las espaldas y preservar la información.</p><p>Rodríguez escribió en 2018 que la adolescente le dijo que “hubo lenguaje y comportamiento inapropiados” por parte de Domínguez en 2017, incluyendo “preguntas y comentarios sobre su vida amorosa y apariencia física”.</p><p>Salvador Cerna, quien supervisó a Domínguez en el Proyecto Resurrección y ahora es su suegro, dijo a WBEZ que nunca “tuvo que disciplinar a Hilario” ni hablar de “sus interacciones con jóvenes”.</p><p>Una portavoz del Proyecto Resurrección dijo que la organización no haría comentarios.</p><p>Rodríguez, quien dijo que era muy amiga de Flores pero que recientemente se pelearon, afirmó que ella no divulgó el informe interno del Proyecto Resurrección. Respaldó su decisión de reportar lo que la joven le contó.</p><p>“Realmente necesitamos responsabilizar específicamente a los hombres”, dijo Rodríguez.</p><p>La representante estatal Theresa Mah, que respaldó a Domínguez en la contienda por el Concejo Municipal de 2019, escuchó los rumores de las acusaciones en su distrito del área de Pilsen. Dijo a WBEZ que habló con el director ejecutivo del Proyecto Resurrección, Raul Raymundo, en 2019 y quedó “satisfecha de que no ocurrió ninguna mala conducta”.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de</i> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a><br></p>

entries.title: Group cheered as woman was sexually assaulted at University of Chicago frat house, police report says
entries.summary: <p>She came to a fraternity party Saturday near the University of Chicago campus, where she told the Chicago police she danced and had some drinks.</p><p>But as Saturday night gave way to Sunday morning, the 21-year-old woman said she “began feeling unwell” and was <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/10/12/woman-21-sexually-assaulted-near-the-university-of-chicago-in-hyde-park" target="_blank" ><u>sexually assaulted at the Alpha Epsilon Pi house</u></a>, 5625 S. University Ave, according to a police report obtained by the Chicago Sun-Times.</p><p>Her account was backed up by two friends, who told the police they intervened by barging into a bathroom as the attack happened.</p><p>The case has placed the University of Chicago, one of the country’s premier academic institutions, at the center of a nationwide reckoning over sexual assault, which has been fueled by another reported attack, this one at a fraternity house at Cornell University in upstate New York.</p><p>On Tuesday afternoon, University of Chicago issued an alert saying that “a person of interest has been identified.” No arrests have been reported.</p><p>The woman’s friends said that a group of men had tried to block them from entering the bathroom after the men were seen “cheering and appearing to encourage the activity inside,” according to the report.</p><p>The group, which consisted of as many as five men, initially told the woman’s friends she wasn’t inside the bathroom, the report says. When the two other women pushed forward, a man grabbed one of them by the hair as the other picked the bathroom lock, according to the report.</p><p>The 21-year-old woman was “not fully conscious” when she was found inside the bathroom, according to the report, which says she and the man were both partially undressed.</p><p>After one of the woman’s friends told him to get off her, “he responded that everything was ‘cool,’ as though nothing had occurred,” the report says.</p><p>When the woman and her friends confronted the man outside the fraternity house, one of the men said they “had identified the wrong person” and pointed the women in another direction and then ran off, according to the report.</p><p>One of the friends gave chase but stopped when she encountered a university police officer, the report says. A complaint was taken, and the 21-year-old was hospitalized.</p><p>The woman who says she was assaulted at the University of Chicago doesn’t attend the school, according to the police report.</p><p>She and her two friends didn’t respond to requests for comment.</p><p>The alert about a person of interest being identified came hours after The Chicago Maroon, the university's independent student newspaper, published <a class="Link" href="https://chicagomaroon.com/54003/news/video-appears-to-show-suspected-perpetrator-of-aepi-party-sexual-assault/" target="_blank" >an article</a> describing a video that appears to show a man matching the suspect's description.</p><p>The suspect was described as a 5-foot-7 male with curly hair and was seen wearing a black, short-sleeve shirt and black pants, according to the police report.</p><p>The alert says the person of interest isn’t affiliated with the University of Chicago. He wasn’t named in the alert because he hasn’t been charged with a crime.</p><p>“This identification has been corroborated by key witness statements and video evidence from University cameras and license plate readers, all of which has been shared with [the Chicago Police Department] by the Department of Safety & Security,” the alert says.</p><p>The university's chapter of Alpha Epsilon Pi said no one affiliated with the fraternity was “involved or complicit with this incident,” according to a statement it posted on Instagram. The chapter said it was working alongside authorities to provide additional details to police.</p><p>The fraternity’s national headquarters said the chapter was told not to hold events or programs until an investigation is done.</p><p>As of Tuesday morning, no one was in custody, police said.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/10/12/woman-21-sexually-assaulted-near-the-university-of-chicago-in-hyde-park" target="_blank" >UChicago frat suspends events after report of sexual assault; students question campus training, Greek life</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Officials probe death of man burned in West Side fire whose car was reported missing
entries.summary: <p>An investigation is underway after a 50-year-old man died was found dead in a basement apartment after a fire early Monday in North Lawndale — and his missing car was found about a mile and a half away.</p><p>About 5:25 a.m., Monday police and firefighters were called to a residential building fire in the 1300 block of South Millard Avenue, police said.</p><p>After the blaze was extinguished, firefighters found the unidentified 50-year-old man unresponsive inside a basement apartment, police said. He was dead at the scene, having been burned over his entire body, according to a police report. </p><p>He also had blood on his chest and blood coming from his ears and mouth. His vehicle was missing from the scene, according to the report, which said no accelerants were found in the apartment. Autopsy results were not immediately available.</p> <p>Investigators located the victim's vehicle in the 1600 block of South California Avenue, on the other side of Douglass Park and about a dozen blocks to the east. They also recovered video footage showing that, at 4:52 a.m. Monday, someone wiped down the inside and outside of the car, then walked away west through the park, the report said. </p><p>No one was displaced by the fire, and no additional injuries were reported, according to police.</p>

entries.title: Trump weighs a public execution, which once elicited delight — and revulsion
entries.summary: <p>A reader writes, aghast at government plans to livestream the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan, the U.S. Army major who murdered 13 fellow soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009.</p><p>"I am so upset, so disgusted and in disbelief," she says. "What has happened to this country?"  </p><p>I want to sympathize, but can't.</p><p>"Disbelief?" I reply. "Really? You are paying attention, right? This is very on brand for them."</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-ae0000" name="module-ae0000"></a> <div class="RichTextSidebarModule-title">Opinion bug</div> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h2>Opinion</h2></div> </div><p>Between condemning children in Africa to death by denying food — and now vaccines — to shooting Americans in the street for failing to comply promptly to the orders of masked men, to the certain atrocities going on out of sight in windowless ICE prisons nationwide, the idea of the government beginning to ballyhoo their horrors has a certain appeal. At least we'll be able to witness this one. And unlike most victims of official violence, Hasan bears undeniable guilt.</p><p>I'm generally against the death penalty, because it is so misapplied, racially and economically. But I'm willing to make exceptions — I'm glad Timothy McVeigh is not still around, writing manifestos, enjoying cheeseburgers and watching Netflix in his cell.  Hasan falls into that category.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-100000" name="image-100000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/0cb608e/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4286x2405+0+295/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Faa%2F9f%2F57f2eeb14691bfdf7d3bc5c724be%2Ffort-hood-shooting-execution-what-to-know.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/f6e7e1d/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4286x2405+0+295/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Faa%2F9f%2F57f2eeb14691bfdf7d3bc5c724be%2Ffort-hood-shooting-execution-what-to-know.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/69e3e84/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4286x2405+0+295/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Faa%2F9f%2F57f2eeb14691bfdf7d3bc5c724be%2Ffort-hood-shooting-execution-what-to-know.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Undated photo provided by the Bell County Sheriff's Department, showing former Army psychiatrist Maj. Nidal Hasan. " srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/69e3e84/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4286x2405+0+295/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Faa%2F9f%2F57f2eeb14691bfdf7d3bc5c724be%2Ffort-hood-shooting-execution-what-to-know.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/caa8b6e/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4286x2405+0+295/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Faa%2F9f%2F57f2eeb14691bfdf7d3bc5c724be%2Ffort-hood-shooting-execution-what-to-know.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/69e3e84/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4286x2405+0+295/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Faa%2F9f%2F57f2eeb14691bfdf7d3bc5c724be%2Ffort-hood-shooting-execution-what-to-know.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Former Army psychiatrist Maj. Nidal Hasan. </p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Uncredited/AP Photos</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Which doesn't mean his death should be served up as public entertainment? Or should it?</p><p>We've fallen out of practice watching public executions. To get myself in the spirit, I pulled down a collection of William Makepeace Thackeray's journalism and reread "Going to See a Man Hanged."</p><p>Writing in 1840, the future author of "Vanity Fair" spends pages setting the scene — his sleepless night before friends arrive in a carriage at 3 a.m., imagining the final hours of "the poor wretch" awaiting execution. The gallows set up in the street before Newgate Prison; the sight sends "a kind of dumb electric shock" through Thackeray. The "gentle and good humored" crowd of 40,000 — Charles Dickens is also there. The cursing ragamuffins and teenage prostitutes, "giggling, drinking, and romping." The jokes, the rumors, the catcalls. </p><p>The condemned man, François Courvoisier, a Swiss valet who slit the throat of his employer, regards the crowd with "a wild, imploring look. His mouth, contracted into a sort of pitiful smile." </p><p>Yet as a nightcap is being drawn over the condemned man's head, and though he'd waited four hours to see it, Thackeray turns away. He writes:</p><p>"I am not ashamed to say that I could look no more, but shut my eyes as the last dreadful act was going on, which sent this wretched, guilty soul in to the presence of God."</p><p>Even unseen, the execution makes Thackeray feel complicit:</p><p>"The sight has left on my mind an extraordinary feeling of terror and shame. It seems to me that I have been abetting an act of frightful wickedness and violence, performed by a set of men against one of their fellows, and I pray God that it may soon be out of the power of any man in England to witness such a hideous and degrading sight."</p><p>It would — though not "soon." The last public execution in England occurred in 1868. The practice ended out of embarrassment over the large, celebratory crowds that gather.</p><p>But not in Burma. In the 1920s, George Orwell, an official of the Indian Imperial Police, witnesses an execution close up.</p><p>It is a "sodden morning of the rains." The condemned man, "a puny wisp of a man, with a shaven head and vague liquid eyes," chained to the belts of his warders, who walk close by him.</p><p>Orwell walks behind, watching, later writing:</p><p>"His feet printed themselves on the wet gravel. And once, in spite of the men who gripped him by each shoulder, he stepped slightly aside to avoid a puddle on the path."</p><p>This small, human gesture gets to Orwell.</p><p>"Till that moment I had never realized what it means to destroy a healthy, conscious man," he writes. "When I saw the prisoner step aside to avoid the puddle, I saw the mystery, the unspeakable wrongness, of cutting a life short when it is in full tide. ... His eyes saw the yellow gravel and the grey walls, and his brain still remembered, foresaw, reasoned — reasoned even about puddles. He and we were a party of men walking together ... and in two minutes, with a sudden snap, one of us would be gone — one mind less, one world less."</p><p>I don't believe I'll watch the livestream Dec. 3, assuming it isn't canceled due to public outcry. No doubt there will be parties, with nachos and beer, among those who don't mind such public entertainment. But I hold out hope that maybe, just as the British public and George Orwell were revolted, maybe some who watch will be disgusted by the spectacle. Maybe this will reach Americans in a way other official excesses haven't.</p>
entries.author: Neil Steinberg

entries.title: Raging Bull roller coaster at Six Flags Great America closed after death at Georgia location
entries.summary: <p>Raging Bull, a roller coaster at Six Flags Great America in Gurnee, is temporarily closed following a fatal incident involving a roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia that left one person dead and several others injured.</p><p>A Six Flags Great America spokesperson confirmed the closure to the Chicago Sun-Times on Tuesday and said there is no timeline for reopening.</p><p>“Out of an abundance of caution, we have temporarily closed similar attractions across our parks,” the spokesperson said in a statement. “The safety of our guests and team members is our highest priority.”</p><p>Raging Bull, which opened in 1999, stands 202 feet tall and stretches 5,057 feet, reaching speeds of up to 73 mph, according to the park's website. It is the tallest and longest coaster in the park. </p><p>The incident in Georgia occurred at approximately 3:58 p.m. Monday at the Georgia park in Cobb County, according to the Cobb County Police Department. Police identified the man who died as Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, 42, of Atlanta. </p><p>Preliminary information gathered through witness and employee interviews indicated Kariem was ejected from the ride and struck other patrons before falling beneath the attraction, police wrote in a press release. The investigation remains ongoing.</p>
entries.author: Misha Manjuran Oberoi

entries.title: Man charged in shooting of 17-year-old in South Lawndale
entries.summary: <p>A man is facing several of charges after being accused of shooting a 17-year-old in South Lawndale last month, according to Chicago police.</p><p>Ricardo Valles, 27, faces charges of attempted first-degree murder, two counts of aggravated battery through discharge of a firearm and a misdemeanor count of criminal damage to property, according to Chicago police. He was arrested Monday.</p><p>Valles is alleged to have shot a 17-year-old who was standing near a sidewalk in the 3800 block of West 30th Street at 3:10 p.m. on Sept. 13, police said. </p><p>The teen was shot in his back and taken to Mount Sinai Hospital in good condition.</p><p>Valles is due in court Wednesday.</p>

entries.title: Ming-Na Wen’s recipe for Popo’s wontons is as good as gold in her family
entries.summary: <p>Wontons hold a special place in my heart. Sitting around our kitchen table making wontons is something I loved doing with my mother as a child.</p><p>Time was scarce, so the chance to make wontons with her became special mother-daughter moments for us. She always had all the fillings ready to go — my favorite was and still is pork, shrimp and vegetables. I'd carefully scoop a bit of filling onto the wonton wrapper and do my best to fold it as neatly as possible.</p><p>Years later, I've continued the tradition with my own children, and together as a family we make Popo’s wontons (“Popo” is the Chinese word for “maternal grandmother”). Just as it was for my mother and me, making wontons gives me and my kids the opportunity to escape the chaos of daily life and bond while we fold 34 together. </p><p>It also gives me the chance to share more about our heritage. For example, the Chinese revere wealth (like most people!). Wontons are a symbol for gold — when folding, your goal is to create a wonton shaped like a Chinese gold ingot. I suppose that’s one way of getting rich. My kids thought it was the silliest, most fun thing to eat “gold.”</p><h3>Popo’s Wontons</h3><p><b>Servings:</b> Makes about 60</p><p><b>Ingredients</b><br>1 (3-inch) nob peeled ginger, minced<br>½ pound large (31 to 40) raw shrimp, shelled and deveined<br>2 tablespoons cornstarch, divided<br>2 teaspoons kosher salt, divided<br>1 pound frozen shepherd's purse, defrosted (or 2 bunches fresh watercress)<br>2 tablespoons light soy sauce<br>1 tablespoon vegetable oil<br>½ teaspoon ground white pepper<br>1 pound ground meat (pork, turkey or chicken)<br>1 large egg<br>2 (12-ounce) packages square, thin wonton wrappers (you won't use them all)</p><p><b>Directions</b></p><p>In a small bowl, soak the ginger in ¼ cup of water for 15 minutes.</p><p>Rinse the shrimp with cold water. Drain them and place in a medium bowl with 1 tablespoon of the cornstarch, massaging it gently into the shrimp to further clean them. Rinse the shrimp again with clean, cold water. Drain them, then toss with ½ teaspoon of the salt. Finely chop the shrimp. Set aside.</p><p>Rinse the defrosted shepherd's purse with cold water, then squeeze out the excess water. Finely chop the greens, then toss them with ½ teaspoon of the salt. Set aside. (If using watercress, boil 2 bunches for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse with cold water. Squeeze out the excess water and finely chop.)</p><p>Remove the ginger from the water and squeeze it over the water to retain as much of the ginger-scented soaking water as possible. Discard the ginger, keeping only the ginger water.</p><p>In a medium nonreactive bowl, combine the ginger water, soy sauce, the remaining 1½ teaspoons of salt, oil, the remaining 1 tablespoon of cornstarch, and the white pepper. Add the ground meat and thoroughly mix it with the seasoning. Add the shrimp and greens and mix everything together. Allow it to marinate, covered in the refrigerator, for 30 minutes. Take a small piece and cook the meat mixture in boiling water until the meat floats, about 3 minutes. Taste it to see if it's seasoned well. If not, then add another teaspoon of salt to the meat and mix well.</p><p>In a small bowl, whisk the egg so that it can be used to seal the wonton skins.</p><p>Fan the stack of skins out to create a pinwheel of skins. This separates the skins, making them easier to pick up. Take one wonton skin and place a dollop of meat mixture (about ½ tablespoon) in the center.</p><p>Using the tip of a butter knife dipped in the egg, brush the top and side edges of the skin. Fold the square in half and gently press edges together. The wonton is now a rectangle. Brush the bottom corners with egg. Holding the rectangle in your palm, bend the left and right corners together toward the center of the wonton. Squeeze the corners together to seal.</p><p>On a tray or plate lined with parchment paper, place the wontons in rows with a bit of separation between them so that they do not stick together. Make sure the tray or plate will fit in your freezer. Once the tray is full, freeze the wontons until the skin feels solid and frozen, about 1 hour. You can then place the wontons in a plastic freezer bag without worrying about them sticking together. Place the bag immediately back into the freezer to further freeze the wontons. Remember to write a date on the bags. They will keep for 3 to 4 months.</p><p>If you're starting with fresh wontons, bring a large pot of water to a boil. Leave enough room in the pot for 1 to 2 cups of additional water. Add the wontons. When the water boils again, add ½ cup cold water. When the water boils again, add another ½ cup of cold water. When wontons float to the top, they are done. Adding cold water in steps like this keeps the skin of the wontons from overcooking and becoming too soft.</p><p>With frozen wontons, repeat the above, but add ½ cup cold water one more time because the frozen meat needs a bit longer to cook through.</p><p><i>Ming-Na Wen is an actor and author of the cookbook "Have You Eaten Yet: Family Recipes From a Restaurant Daughter."</i></p><p><i>Excerpted from "Have You Eaten Yet? Family Recipes From a Restaurant Daughter." Copyright 2026 by Ming-Na Wen. Reproduced by permission of Simon Element, an imprint of Simon & Schuster. All rights reserved.</i></p>

entries.title: New lawsuits allege decades of child sex abuse at former Holy Angels parish
entries.summary: <p>The Archdiocese of Chicago is facing new allegations over its treatment of Black Catholic children who were sexually abused by priests at a former South Side parish.</p><p>Seven lawsuits filed Tuesday allege the Archdiocese knew about sexual abuse at the former Holy Angels Parish in Bronzeville.</p><p>“Holy Angels was not a sanctuary for children, it was a sanctuary for sexual predators protected by the Chicago Archdiocese,” attorney Steven Hart, who is representing the victims, said at a news conference.</p><p>Attorneys at Hart McLaughlin & Eldridge allege that more than 100 Black children, some as young as 5, were sexually abused by priests at the former parish and school over several decades. On Tuesday, the attorneys filed lawsuits on behalf of seven alleged victims, with plans to file dozens more.</p><p>Hart said they are seeking compensation for the trauma their clients suffered at the hands of the accused priests, as well as an acknowledgment from the Archdiocese that it failed to protect them.</p><p>“For decades, the institution that was supposed to be a sanctuary for family and children became a place where their innocence was stolen,” said Hart.</p><p>The Archdiocese of Chicago told the Sun-Times it did not comment on lawsuits.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> Kenneth Brigham.</p><p>Only Calicott is named in the Archdiocese’s Clergy Substantiated <a class="Link" href="https://protect.archchicago.org/documents/351902/3447104/Clergy+Substantiated+Allegations+List/34ce5b18-819f-4c0a-909e-8e0c3121243a" target="_blank" >Allegations List</a>.</p><p>Attorney Sean O'Malley claimed the abuse at the parish was “a consequence of the Archdiocese of Chicago's fear of George Clements's political potency.”</p><p>Clements, who <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2019/11/25/20981924/george-clements-died-catholic-priest-archdiocese-obituary" target="_blank" >died in 2019</a>, was a longtime civil rights advocate on the South Side and was known as the first Catholic priest to adopt a child. Months before his death, he was accused of sexually abusing a minor in 1974 and claimed the allegation was “totally unfounded.”</p><p>But O’Malley called Clements an imposter and “probably the most He was permanently removed from the ministry in 2002. But attorneys said the action came “too late” for their client, who was sexually abused at Holy Angels after 1995.</p><p>Although priests have been accused of sexually abusing children across Chicago, attorneys said it was “hard to ignore the race element” of the abuse at Holy Angels.</p><p>“It is our allegation that when you discriminate against children, against victims of child sex abuse through your indifference or your assessment of their credibility, you are discriminating against them based on race. We regard that as a form of malice,” said O’Malley.</p>

entries.title: The only gubernatorial debate between Gov. Pritzker and Darren Bailey is tonight. Here's how to watch.
entries.summary: <p>In the second round of their <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-llinois-governor-race-jb-pritzker-darren-bailey-collin-corbett" target="_blank" ><u>gubernatorial rematch</u></a>, incumbent Democratic Gov. JB Pritzker will go head-to-head with Republican nominee Darren Bailey Tuesday night in their only debate of the 2026 election season.</p><p>The billionaire two-term governor squares off with the former downstate legislator and farmer at 8 p.m. for the <a class="Link" href="https://www.youtube.com/@wttw/streams" target="_blank" >WTTW News Gubernatorial Forum</a>, which will also air on WBEZ 91.5 FM.</p><p>Pritzker faces a familiar opponent in <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/13/jb-pritzker-darren-bailey-collin-corbett-illinois-governor-election-november-midterm" target="_blank" ><u>his bid for a rare third term</u></a>, four years after beating Bailey by nearly 13 percentage points.</p><p>Bailey’s main goal will be to win over Chicago-area voters who soundly rejected him in a 2022 election season that was largely defined by his branding of the city as a “hellhole” during a televised primary debate.</p><p>This time around, Bailey has tried to pin cost-of-living increases on Pritzker, who blames President Donald Trump for most of those affordability concerns — and is keen to remind voters that Bailey is a longtime Trump supporter.</p><p>Not invited to participate in Tuesday’s forum was independent candidate Collin Corbett, who slammed his exclusion based on poll numbers.</p><p>“While the major party candidates call each other names, debate evolution, and fight over which is more extreme, I’m the only candidate providing actual solutions to the problems working families face,” Corbett said in a statement. “By keeping me off the forum stage, WTTW is depriving the public of hearing plans to lower property taxes, fully fund education, get our state growing again, and raise everyone’s wages.”</p>
entries.author: Mitchell Armentrout

entries.title: Chicago man charged with attempted murder in Oak Lawn stabbing
entries.summary: <p>A Chicago man is facing attempted murder charges in Oak Lawn stabbing, according to Oak Lawn police.</p><p>Michael Duplessis Jr., 42, is charged with attempted first degree murder, police said.</p><p>Duplessis was in an argument with another man, who had asked him to leave the area near a Jewel-Osco at 8757 South Ridgeland Ave., when Duplessis allegedly spat on him before they physically fought, police said. Duplessis then allegedly stabbed him multiple times.</p><p>The injured man was taken to Christ Medical Center in critical condition where he underwent emergency surgery, police said.</p><p>Duplessis was ordered held awaiting trial at a detention hearing Monday, police said. He’s due back in court Wednesday.</p><p>He was previously charged in November 2025 with aggravated battery of a victim over 60-years-old, for which he was sentenced to a year in prison, according to court records. </p><p>Duplessis was given credit for 194 days served while the trial was ongoing, and was released earlier this year.</p>
entries.author: Sun-Times Wire

entries.title: 2 charged in Stevenson Expressway road rage shooting
entries.summary: <p>Two Chicago residents were arrested and charged in a September shooting on the Stevenson Expressway, according to Illinois State Police.</p><p>Pedro Anzaldua, 28, is charged with attempted murder, aggravated discharge of a firearm and aggravated assault, police said. Janie Palomo, 32, was also charged with misdemeanor aggravated assault with a firearm.</p><p>Around 11 p.m. on Sept. 5, police said they received reports of two people on a motorcycle in the I-55 southbound lanes just north of I-294 firing shots at another vehicle during a road rage incident, police said. No injuries were reported.</p><p>They were arrested Sunday after being located by the Blue Island Police Department, though only Anzaldua remains in custody awaiting a detention hearing, police said.</p>
entries.author: Sun-Times Wire
